mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome. I'm so glad you're here, joining me for a journey that asks some tough, honest questions about race, language, and justice in America. Have you ever wondered how the words we use—especially the ones loaded with history and pain—can shape the very way justice is delivered? Or how identity itself can tip the scales in a courtroom, even when the law claims to be neutral? Together, we're about to explore these ideas through the lens of Jody Armour’s thought-provoking book, N*gga Theory: Race, Language, Unequal Justice, and the Law. This isn’t just about legal theory—it’s about the lived realities of people whose stories often go unheard. We’ll dig deep into how language doesn’t just reflect bias, but can actually reinforce and deepen the inequalities already woven into our justice system. Along the way, we’ll challenge old assumptions about what makes someone “guilty” or “innocent,” and ask who really gets to define right and wrong—and at what cost. Get ready to reconsider what you think you know about blame, punishment, and the line between personal responsibility and systemic oppression. I invite you to keep an open mind as we question how words become weapons, and how rethinking their power might open the door to empathy, understanding, and much-needed reform. So, let’s dive in together and see what new possibilities we can discover at the crossroads of language and justice.
